section: RMIT University case study: bringing a multi-country AV and UC estate under Symphony monitoring
body:
RMIT University (Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology) uses AVI-SPL's Symphony to monitor its networked AV and collaboration systems across campuses in several countries. The case study is proof of Symphony working at large scale in education. The page lists the locations as Melbourne, Australia, Vietnam, Indonesia, China, Singapore and Spain.

**Who and why**

- RMIT is described as ranked among the top 250 universities in the world, and its users depend on classroom technology for learning.
- It had to support thousands of technology devices from various manufacturers. Having technicians check every device by hand, or waiting for users to ask for AV support, is described as inefficient, unscalable and disruptive.
- Before Symphony, RMIT used multiple applications and could reach only about 10% of its AV estate for online monitoring.
- Shane Somerville, head of managed services for Connected Vision Group, said this was a problem because classes were disrupted and teaching time was wasted.

**What was put in place**

- Symphony is AVI-SPL's proprietary User Experience Management Application. The platform is cloud-based and mobile-friendly.
- RMIT staff use it to monitor the status of meeting rooms, classrooms and other areas with networked AV and collaboration systems, in a single-pane view for IT and AV support teams.
- RMIT now has, for the first time, sight of how its networked AV infrastructure is operating across multiple campuses in different countries.
- Scale as stated: the monitored estate is over 4,600+ devices in over 1,000 rooms and 100+ buildings worldwide. Symphony proactively alerts technicians so issues can be resolved before students and staff are affected.

**Day one incident**

Hundreds of rooms and thousands of devices were onboarded into Symphony over a weekend. On the Monday morning technicians were notified that all AV and UC devices in one campus building were unreachable. They isolated the single failure point and fixed it well before classes started, with no disruption to students or staff. The page headline says the network issue would have affected 5,000+ students.

**The partnership**

Connected Vision Group is an alliance of commercial AV service and solution providers that partners with AVI-SPL on projects based out of Australia and New Zealand. One member, InSight Systems, is the provider of AV support services to RMIT University. InSight Systems and AVI-SPL worked closely together on the solution. Luke Hogan, RMIT AV operations manager, Connected Vision Group, said AVI-SPL had been there at every step for anything they asked for or needed help with.

**When to use this**

Use it when a customer asks for evidence of Symphony monitoring a large, multi-site or multi-country estate, or for an education example of moving from reactive to proactive AV support.
